key_insight: In children with PANS, pain and fatigue are common and can progress to fibromyalgia-like syndromes, especially when symptom burden is already high at presentation.
clinical_relevance: Early recognition of widespread pain and fatigue in PANS may help identify patients at higher risk for persistent symptoms and guide closer follow-up.
method: Prospective observational cohort of 204 consecutive PANS patients at a Stanford clinic.
Symptoms were measured with the 2016 ACR Fibromyalgia Survey Questionnaire, including WPI and SSS.
Clinician-recorded pain syndromes were identified by retrospective medical record review; Cox proportional hazards models assessed predictors of progression.
evidence_signal: In this cohort, 42% met threshold scores for fibromyalgia criteria at least once during follow-up, and 13.7% progressed to full ACR fibromyalgia criteria; higher baseline WPI and SSS predicted faster progression.
watch_item: This single-center observational study can show association, not causation, and the clinic-based sample may limit generalizability.
paper_title: Prevalence and Predictors of Pain and Fatigue in Pediatric Acute-Onset Neuropsychiatric Syndrome (PANS)
